newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian 88 CEO says not pulling offer.
newsitem.headline: Canadian 88 CEO says not pulling offer.

text.p: Canadian 88 Energy Corp chief executive Greg Noval said on Wednesday he had no plans to pull his C$652 million bid for Morrison Petroleums Ltd off the table.
Noval said in a telephone interview from Toronto that he believed a drop in Morrison's share price today resulted from arbitragers betting that no rival suitor for Morrison was in the wings.
"We had a meeting this morning with the arbs in New York and the game's up on Morrison -- there's no white knight," he said. "The stock's coming in line with our bid."
Canadian 88 has offered C$10 cash a share for up to C$140 million of the total price. The rest would be made up with a share swap of 1.5 Canadian 88 shares for each Morrison share.
But with Canadian 88 trading at 5.95, the exchange value would be C$8.93 a share.
Noval said he believed that Morrison's share price would likely soon fall below C$10.
Paul Charron, Morrison's vice-president of finance, said on Wednesday that interest from several companies in launching a rival bid remained strong.

"I've been speaking to many of the arbs this morning and continue to do so to let them know that we are pursuing alternatives here...and that our data room is very active and we are talking to several interested parties," Charron said.
